notes: The roster is the 14-star HVS1/HVS4-HVS16 sample, treated as a follow-up sample from the combined Brown et al. (2007b, 2008) surveys (T:p1-b13, T:p1-b18). HVS2 is marked in Fig. 1 (I:p2-b0) but explicitly excluded from the analysis (T:p1-b15), so it is not rostered. HD 271791 is only cited as a known unbound hyper-runaway contaminant (T:p1-b8, T:p2-b12), not analyzed as a survey star. The four 'possible HVSs' and eight 'possibly bound HVSs' mentioned at T:p2-b5 are not individually identified in the supplied text.

HVS1: The paper identifies HVS1 as part of the new HVS survey (T:p1-b18) and plots it in the Galactic-coordinate map (I:p2-b0), but it does not report any numerical right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability specifically for HVS1. No eligible quantity could therefore be extracted.

HVS4: LOCATION T:p1-b18 identifies HVS4 only as part of the original survey's HVS4-HVS10, and LOCATION T:p1-b15 states that the combined survey contains 14 HVSs; LOCATION I:p2-b0 marks HVS4's sky position in a polar plot. The supplied paper reports no individual numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS4.

HVS5: HVS5 is identified only as part of the original HVS survey sample (HVS4-HVS10; T:p1-b18) and is plotted among the 14 unbound HVSs in Figure 1 (I:p2-b0, with caption at T:p2-b0). The paper gives no individual numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS5. Figure 1 shows Galactic longitude and latitude positions, not equatorial coordinates, and no numeric coordinates are provided for HVS5.

HVS6: HVS6 is identified as one of the HVS4-HVS10 stars in the original survey (T:p1-b18) and is marked in the Galactic-coordinate polar projection (I:p2-b0). The paper does not report numerical equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS6. The plotted position is in Galactic longitude and latitude, which are not among the requested quantity identifiers, so no requested quantity can be extracted for this star.

HVS7: HVS7 is discussed only in connection with its angular position and pair with HVS15. Text at T:p2-b8 states that HVS7 and HVS15 are near Galactic coordinates (l,b)=(265°,55°) and are separated by 2.5°, but these are not equatorial right ascension/declination and no eligible distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported numerically for HVS7. Figure 1 at I:p2-b0 also shows only angular positions in Galactic coordinates. Therefore no listed quantity can be extracted for HVS7 without unsupported conversion or inference.

HVS8: HVS8 is identified only as one of the original-survey HVSs (HVS4–HVS10; T:p1-b18) and is labeled in the polar sky map in Fig. 1 (I:p2-b0). The paper does not report individual coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS8, so no quantities are retained.

HVS9: HVS9 is mentioned only as part of the original survey sample (HVS4–HVS10) at T:p1-b18 and is marked in Fig. 1 (I:p2-b0), but the paper does not report quantitative astrometric, distance, velocity, Galactic-radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability values for HVS9.

HVS10: HVS10 is identified only as part of the original HVS survey sample (HVS4-HVS10) at T:p1-b18 and is marked in Figure 1 (I:p2-b0). The paper does not report individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS10; the numerical results presented are sample-level anisotropy statistics.

HVS11: HVS11 is identified only as part of the new HVS survey (HVS1 and HVS11-HVS16; T:p1-b18) and is plotted among the 14 unbound HVSs in Fig. 1 (I:p2-b0). The paper reports no individual coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS11, so no quantities are extracted.

HVS12: The 429 km/s value is reported as a “minimum rest-frame velocity”; I recorded it as a lower bound on galactic_rest_frame_velocity rather than radial_velocity because the rules exclude velocities relative to the Galactic standard of rest. The paper gives only an approximate Galactic coordinate (l,b) for the HVS12 pair region and no numerical distance for HVS12, so no ra/dec or distance is extracted (T:p2-b8).

HVS13: HVS13 is discussed only in the HVS-pair analysis (T:p2-b8). The text places HVS12 & HVS13 near (l,b) = (245°, 52°), but gives no individual right ascension or declination. It states that HVS12 has a 429 km/s minimum rest-frame velocity “very similar” to HVS13 and HVS14 and half the distance of those two, but gives no numeric velocity or distance specifically for HVS13. Figure 1 (I:p2-b0) labels HVS13 but provides no tabulated coordinate or velocity value. Therefore no eligible numeric value for the requested quantities is reported for HVS13.

HVS14: HVS14 is mentioned in T:p2-b8 only as part of a close pair with HVS12 near Galactic (l, b) = (245°, 52°), and in a qualitative comparison of its distance and minimum rest-frame velocity with HVS12 and HVS13. No eligible equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or numeric bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS14.

HVS15: The target HVS15 is identified as an unbound HVS and is located in Figure 1 (I:p2-b0), but the paper only gives a Galactic-coordinate vicinity in T:p2-b8: HVS7 & HVS15 are “near (l,b)=(265°,55°)” and separated by 2.5°. No equatorial right ascension/declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported numerically for HVS15. The statement that HVS7 & HVS15 have velocities and distances implying a ~70 Myr travel-time difference does not provide individual values. Its unbound classification is not a probability and therefore is not entered under unbound_probability.

HVS16: HVS16 is identified only as a member of the new HVS survey (“HVS1 and HVS11–HVS16”; T:p1-b18) and is marked in the Galactic-coordinate polar plot in Fig. 1 (I:p2-b0). The paper reports no individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS16. Figure 1 does not provide numeric per-star coordinates or velocities, so no quantity can be extracted without calculation or external assumptions.
